tiles.label: The First Step
tiles.defaultTopic: the moment before doing the hard thing
tiles.promptSeed: Write about the moment right before someone does something that scares them — not the outcome, just the internal decision to take the first step despite the fear.
tiles.description: The moment before doing the hard thing, and the decision to do it anyway.
constraints: End at the moment of the step, not the result

tiles.label: Facing It
tiles.promptSeed: Write about someone finally confronting something they've been avoiding — a conversation, a fear, a truth — with honesty about how hard it is, without minimizing the difficulty.
tiles.description: Turning to look directly at the thing you've been avoiding.
constraints: No forced resolution or tidy lesson

tiles.label: Standing Alone
tiles.defaultTopic: holding a position when no one else will
tiles.promptSeed: Write about someone holding to a decision or belief while standing genuinely alone in it, focusing on what it costs them and why they hold the line anyway.
tiles.description: Holding a position when no one else will stand with you.

tiles.label: The Harder Right
tiles.defaultTopic: choosing the honest path when no one's watching
tiles.promptSeed: Write about a small, private decision where the easier option was available and the harder, more honest option was chosen instead, with no one else there to witness it.
tiles.description: Choosing the difficult, honest path over the easy one.
constraints: No audience for the choice — it's private

tiles.label: Starting Over
tiles.defaultTopic: the first ordinary day of beginning again
tiles.promptSeed: Write about the first small, unremarkable day of starting over after a significant loss or failure — not the dramatic decision to start over, but the quiet mechanics of the first day doing it.
tiles.description: The first ordinary day of beginning again.
constraints: Focus on small concrete actions, not internal monologue about hope

tiles.label: The Apology
tiles.defaultTopic: saying the hard thing, and meaning it
tiles.promptSeed: Write about someone delivering a genuine, specific apology for something they got wrong, focusing on the discomfort of accountability rather than the relief afterward.
tiles.description: Saying the hard thing, and meaning it.
constraints: The apology must be specific, not generic

tiles.label: New Beginning
tiles.defaultTopic: standing at the edge of something new
tiles.promptSeed: Write about someone standing at the literal or figurative threshold of a new beginning — a new place, role, or chapter — capturing both the uncertainty and the willingness to step forward.
tiles.description: Standing at the edge of something new, uncertain but willing.

tiles.label: What I Know Now
tiles.promptSeed: Write in first person as someone reflecting on a past mistake or hard period, articulating what they understand now that they didn't then, without excessive self-criticism.
tiles.description: Looking back at who you were, with hard-won understanding.

tiles.label: One Day at a Time
tiles.defaultTopic: getting through today, which is enough
tiles.promptSeed: Write about someone getting through one ordinary, difficult day — not solving everything, just making it through — and finding that enough.
tiles.description: Getting through today, which is enough for today.

tiles.label: The Little Win
tiles.defaultTopic: a small accomplishment that matters more than it looks
tiles.promptSeed: Write about a small, easily-overlooked accomplishment — finishing a task, making a call, getting out of bed — and why it matters more than its size suggests, given what it took to do it.
tiles.description: A small accomplishment that matters more than it looks like it should.

tiles.label: Progress, Not Perfection
tiles.defaultTopic: doing it imperfectly, and doing it anyway
tiles.promptSeed: Write about someone doing something imperfectly — a skill, a habit, a piece of work — and choosing to value the attempt and the progress over getting it exactly right.
tiles.description: Doing it imperfectly, and doing it anyway.

tiles.label: Today I Showed Up
tiles.defaultTopic: just showing up, on a day when that was hard
tiles.promptSeed: Write in first person, brief, about simply showing up for something — work, a commitment, a person — on a day when not showing up would have been easier, without dramatizing it.
tiles.description: Just showing up, on a day when that was hard.

[MODE]

[TILE]

[CONSTRAINTS]
- Output ONLY the creative piece — nothing else.
- Follow the structural rules of the selected form exactly (paragraph and sentence limits).
- Maintain a sincere, grounded emotional register.
- Avoid generic motivational-poster phrasing and forced resolutions.
